query: For MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials, what single intervention could improve mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected changes relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Partial substitution of Si with Ge in MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials will improve mechanical performance (e.g., ductility, fracture toughness) while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect, due to reduced lattice distortion and preserved magnetostructural transition.
generation.material_initial_state: MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration material in polycrystalline form, with nominal composition MnNiSi.
generation.intervention: Partial substitution of Si with Ge (e.g., MnNiSi1-xGex, with x ≈ 0.1–0.2).
generation.conditions: Room temperature to near the magnetostructural transition temperature; polycrystalline bulk samples; ambient pressure.
generation.structural_mediator: Ge substitution reduces lattice mismatch and internal strain, improving grain boundary cohesion and mechanical properties, while maintaining the first-order magnetostructural transition.
generation.mechanism: Ge atoms, being larger than Si, relieve lattice strain and reduce brittleness, while their similar electronic structure preserves the magnetic exchange interactions responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to baseline MnNiSi, MnNiSi1-xGex samples will show higher fracture toughness and ductility, with only minor reduction (≤10%) in peak magnetocaloric effect (ΔS_M).
generation.baseline: Polycrystalline MnNiSi without Ge substitution, known for large magnetocaloric effect but poor mechanical performance (brittleness).
generation.boundary: If Ge content exceeds x ≈ 0.2, magnetocaloric effect may decrease significantly due to disruption of magnetostructural transition.
generation.uncertainty: Exact quantitative improvement in mechanical properties and retention of magnetocaloric effect is uncertain without experimental data; effect size is estimated based on analogous substitutions in similar systems.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare MnNiSi and MnNiSi1-xGex (x ≈ 0.1–0.2) polycrystalline samples. Measure fracture toughness and ductility (e.g., via three-point bending or compression tests), and magnetocaloric effect (ΔS_M) near the transition temperature using magnetization and calorimetry.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If MnNiSi1-xGex samples do not show improved mechanical performance (≥10% increase in fracture toughness or ductility) or if peak ΔS_M decreases by more than 10% compared to MnNiSi, the hypothesis is falsified.
